source.title: When Do LLMs Need Human Experts? Evidence for Social Science from Jurisprudential Classification
source.authors: Caroline Cheng; Edward H. Stiglitz; D. Mimno; Matthew Wilkens

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates downstream classification across models and reports that scaling alone does not solve this task. It does not test the language-model pretraining-loss scaling laws or fit compute-optimal allocations.
record.gate_note: The study reports jurisprudential-classification F1 scores for prompted and fine-tuned models, which bear on V6. It does not measure held-out pretraining cross-entropy, fit scaling curves, or vary compute budgets to find optimal parameter/token splits. Kaplan et al. is cited as background, not tested. Rows record multiclass macro F1 by model and prompt strategy; the detailed class-specific metrics and the separate binary-task results are not included because they do not establish a pretraining-loss or compute-scaling relation.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates LLMs of many sizes on a specialized legal classification task. The only clean within-family size comparison is Llama-3.1-Instruct 8B vs 70B, prompted and fine-tuned. This bears weakly on V6 (downstream performance improving with scale) in a new setting. It is T3 rather than T5: the authors' 'scaling alone does not solve this task' is about frontier models trailing fine-tuned BERT, not an argument that scale-performance relations fail. No pretraining loss, compute, or fitted curves are reported.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that frontier-scale prompted LLMs still underperform fine-tuned BERT on this expert task. All fine-tuned LLMs improve over their prompted versions, but only fine-tuned GPT-4.1 and 70B-class models surpass BERT. BERT remains a cost-effective alternative, so expert annotation is still needed. They note the single domain, the single split for fine-tuned generative models, and that the labeled-data budget was not varied.
record.recipe_differences: This is a downstream jurisprudential-classification evaluation, not a language-model pretraining loss sweep or compute-optimal scaling-law fit. Models are evaluated using prompting and supervised fine-tuning.
record.method_sensitivity: Prompting strategy changes reported macro F1; fine-tuning regime also changes results. Prompted and fine-tuned generative models use five splits and one split, respectively.

fits_no_version.finding: Even the largest prompted frontier models (GPT-5.2, 0.68) underperform fine-tuned LEGAL-BERT (0.71). Only fine-tuned GPT-4.1 and 70B-class models surpass it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: On expert-domain classification, model scale with prompting alone does not reach fine-tuned small encoder performance.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the Seventh Workshop on Natural Language Processing and Computational Social Science
record.problems: Only one specialized domain is studied. Fine-tuned generative models are evaluated on a single split, and the paper reports no error bars or uncertainty estimates for these scores. Model families and variants are not a controlled parameter-scaling series; pretraining loss and compute are not measured.
record.rows_left_out: Class-specific precision, recall, and F1 results in Table B.1 and binary-task scores in Table B.2 are not extracted; the rows focus on the multiclass macro-F1 evidence relevant to downstream performance. Table 1's best-strategy summary duplicates results represented by the strategy-specific scores in Table B.1.

untested.parts: No shape comparisons at fixed parameter count.
No other modality or regime scaling fits.
No predictive curve, no link to pretraining loss, and only two sizes in one family (Llama 8B/70B); Qwen and cross-family comparisons are confounded.

missing.what: Binary-task macro F1 for Llama-3.1 8B vs 70B: prompted 0.60 vs 0.69; fine-tuned 0.78 vs 0.78.
Fine-tuned BERT baselines (0.70-0.71 macro F1), the reference point for the authors' scaling statement.

record.verdict_notes: Kaplan et al. is cited only as background. The authors' 'scaling' refers to frontier vs small models in general, not a measured scale curve. Qwen 30B/80B are MoE models with about 3B active parameters, so their total size is not a clean scale variable. No uncertainty is reported; differences of 0.01-0.02 are treated as negligible.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss or loss-versus-parameters, tokens, or compute measurement.
No small-run fit or prediction of larger-run pretraining loss.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or comparison of optimal parameter and token counts.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
No scaling-law tests in other modalities or training regimes.
The study evaluates one downstream classification task; it does not relate downstream performance to pretraining loss or fit a predictive scale-performance curve.
No scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal split are fitted or compared across setups.

relationships.reason: 70B is no better than 8B with descriptions and examples (r04/r05, r13/r14), and worse with CoT, 0.43 to 0.33 (r22/r23).
relationships.display_finding: The 70B model performed no better than 8B with descriptions and examples, while chain-of-thought scores fell from 0.43 to 0.33.

relationships.condition: Fine-tuned Llama-3.1-Instruct 8B vs 70B, multiclass task, single split
relationships.reason: 70B beats 8B under all three prompt formats: 0.61 to 0.66, 0.59 to 0.74, 0.65 to 0.76 (r29/r30, r34/r35, r39/r40). These are single-split results.
relationships.display_finding: Scores increase from 0.61 to 0.66, 0.59 to 0.74, and 0.65 to 0.76 across the three prompt formats on a single split.

relationships.condition: Binary interpretation task, Llama-3.1 8B vs 70B (Table B.2, not in rows)
relationships.reason: From the text, not rows: prompted 70B improves over 8B (0.60 to 0.69), but fine-tuned 8B and 70B tie at 0.78. The scale benefit flips between regimes and tasks.
relationships.display_finding: Prompted accuracy rose from 0.60 at 8B to 0.69 at 70B, while both fine-tuned sizes scored 0.78.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: The 70B model scores below the 8B model with descriptions and chain-of-thought, while the examples condition shows only a small increase (r04-r05, r13-r14, r22-r23).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The 70B model scores higher than the 8B model in all three prompt conditions, although these are single-split results (r29-r30, r34-r35, r39-r40).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Fine-tuned Qwen variants, matched prompt strategies
reader_labels.reason: The 30B variant has only small macro-F1 increases over the 4B variant, and the models are different variants rather than a controlled scale series (r31-r32, r36-r37, r41-r42).
